SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #7 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What does the letter E stand for on a compass rose? (1 mark)
   A. Earth
   B. Equator
   C. East
   D. Edge

2. What should you find first when you read a map? (1 mark)
   A. The colours
   B. The north arrow
   C. The size of the paper
   D. The names of rivers

3. Which word describes a picture that shows the four cardinal points? (1 mark)
   A. Rain gauge
   B. Weather chart
   C. Compass rose
   D. Timeline

4. What do we call the smaller parts into which a sub-county is divided? (1 mark)
   A. Plateaus
   B. Wards
   C. Oceans
   D. Continents

5. Which imaginary line crosses Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. The boundary
   B. The river line
   C. The equator
   D. The railway line

6. What does the size of a county mean? (1 mark)
   A. The number of people in it
   B. The area of land it covers
   C. The number of roads in it
   D. The number of schools in it

7. What is a valley? (1 mark)
   A. A huge flat plain
   B. Low land between hills or mountains
   C. A very high peak
   D. A big lake

8. Which of these uses the water of a river to make electricity? (1 mark)
   A. A hydroelectric power station
   B. A church
   C. A school
   D. A market

9. Where does a river usually start? (1 mark)
   A. In the desert
   B. On high land
   C. On the beach
   D. In a lake

10. Which of these is one of the four seasons in the county? (1 mark)
   A. Rainy season
   B. Autumn
   C. Spring
   D. Winter

11. What is a season? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of clothing
   B. A type of crop
   C. A part of the year with a typical kind of weather
   D. The weather on one day

12. On a weather chart, which symbol usually means a sunny day? (1 mark)
   A. A sun
   B. A cloud
   C. A wind arrow
   D. A raindrop

13. What is a historic built environment? (1 mark)
   A. A river
   B. A natural forest
   C. A place built long ago that tells us about the past
   D. A new shopping mall

14. What should you do when visiting a museum? (1 mark)
   A. Take objects home
   B. Shout loudly
   C. Run around the halls
   D. Listen to the guide and do not touch objects unless allowed

15. Which of these is not a historic built environment? (1 mark)
   A. A monument
   B. A cultural centre
   C. A natural river
   D. A museum

16. In a chart of who gives and who needs, what does a farmer give? (1 mark)
   A. Health care
   B. Food
   C. Learning
   D. Transport

17. Why can no person do every job alone? (1 mark)
   A. There are too many skills and jobs to learn
   B. People are lazy
   C. Money is not needed
   D. Jobs are not important

18. What is harambee? (1 mark)
   A. A school subject
   B. A type of crop
   C. A kind of market
   D. Working together to solve a problem

19. On a dot map where one dot means 1,000 people, an area has 7 dots. How many people live there? (1 mark)
   A. 70,000
   B. 7,000
   C. 700
   D. 70

20. What do we call an area where few people live in a large space? (1 mark)
   A. Sparsely populated
   B. Densely populated
   C. Busy
   D. Crowded

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Give two reasons why some areas are sparsely populated. (2 marks)

22. Explain why a mountain can be a source of water for people living far away. (3 marks)

23. Explain four ways in which rainy weather makes roads dangerous. (4 marks)

24. A pupil stands facing east. Say what is behind the pupil, on the left and on the right. (3 marks)

25. Give two examples of goods and two examples of services. (4 marks)

26. Name the four seasons in the county. (2 marks)

27. Explain how the four seasons can influence what people do in your county. Give one example for each season. (5 marks)

28. County A covers 15 grid squares and County B covers 9 grid squares. Which is larger and by how many squares? Show your working. (3 marks)

29. Explain the difference between a physical feature and a built feature. Give one example of each. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #7 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — East
   E is the short form of east.

2. B — The north arrow
   Finding north first helps you read all other directions.

3. C — Compass rose
   A compass rose shows N, E, S and W.

4. B — Wards
   Sub-counties are divided into wards.

5. C — The equator
   The equator crosses the middle of Kenya.

6. B — The area of land it covers
   Size means the area of land, not the population.

7. B — Low land between hills or mountains
   A valley is a low area between higher land.

8. A — A hydroelectric power station
   Hydroelectric stations use falling river water to make electricity.

9. B — On high land
   Rivers start on high land and flow to lower land.

10. A — Rainy season
   The four seasons are hot, cold, dry and rainy.

11. C — A part of the year with a typical kind of weather
   A season is the weather that is typical over several months.

12. A — A sun
   A sun symbol shows sunny weather.

13. C — A place built long ago that tells us about the past
   Historic built places are old places made by people.

14. D — Listen to the guide and do not touch objects unless allowed
   Good manners protect the objects and other visitors.

15. C — A natural river
   A river is a natural feature, not built by people.

16. B — Food
   Farmers give food to the community.

17. A — There are too many skills and jobs to learn
   Nobody can grow all food, teach, heal and build alone.

18. D — Working together to solve a problem
   Harambee means pulling together.

19. B — 7,000
   7 x 1,000 = 7,000.

20. A — Sparsely populated
   Sparse means thinly spread.

SECTION B
----
21. (2 marks)
   Answer: Very little rain and no water, and thick forests, swamps or steep land. Accept game parks or few roads.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: Mountains catch rain. The rain flows into rivers. Rivers carry the water to farms and towns far away.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

23. (4 marks)
   Answer: Roads become slippery, it is harder to see, floods can sweep away people and vehicles, and water can hide holes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: Behind is west. On the left is north. On the right is south.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct direction.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: Goods: maize and shoes. Services: teaching and nursing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct example.

26. (2 marks)
   Answer: Hot, cold, dry and rainy.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for all four, 1 mark for two or three.

27. (5 marks)
   Answer: Rainy: farmers plant crops. Dry: farmers harvest and dry crops. Hot: people drink more water and wear light clothes. Cold: people wear warm clothes and drink hot tea. Award a fifth mark for a clear explanation of why seasons matter for farming.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each season example and 1 mark for the link to activities.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: County A is larger by 6 squares.
   Working / marking points: 15 - 9 = 6. 1 mark for choosing A, 1 mark for subtracting, 1 mark for 6 squares.

29. (4 marks)
   Answer: A physical feature is natural, such as a mountain. A built feature is made by people, such as a bridge.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for each correct example.
